author: Associated Press
description:
State DMV says vehicles pose ‘imminent hazard’ after cars entered closed zone and tried to bypass highway patrol

California has banned Waymo’s autonomous vehicles from state freeways, saying they pose an “imminent hazard” after a spate of recent incidents.

The restrictions, issued last Wednesday, bar Waymo from “operating or testing its  driverless vehicles on all California freeways,” Jonathan Groveman, a spokesperson for the state’s department of motor vehicles, said in a statement.

Continue reading...
title: California bans Waymo self-driving cars from freeways

author: Natricia Duncan Caribbean correspondent
description:
St Kitts and Nevis to wind down citizenship-by-investment program after EU warns of end to visa-free access

The decision by St Kitts and Nevis to end a lucrative programme offering citizenship to wealthy foreigners in exchange for investment threatens its economy and ability to support people in need, the premier of the island of Nevis has warned.

On Friday, Terrance Drew, the prime minister of the twin-island Caribbean nation, announced he would wind down the citizenship-by-investment (CBI) programme, after the European Union threatened to end visa-free access for St Kitts and Nevis.

Continue reading...
title: Caribbean nations fear economic impact of shuttering citizenship program after EU threats

author: Australian Associated Press
description:
Stuart Ramsey says it is a ‘bloody disgrace’ the gelding was left in the skip bin while awaiting burial

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

So You Are’s owner-breeder has demanded a full investigation after the Melbourne Cup runner’s body was found in a skip at a Sydney tip, insisting “heads have got to roll”.

Stuart Ramsey says it is a “bloody disgrace” the gelding was left in the skip bin while awaiting burial at Sydney’s Cleanaway Lucas Heights Resource Recovery Centre.

Continue reading...
title: ‘Heads should roll’: owner of Melbourne Cup horse found dumped in skip bin demands probe

author: Cecilia Nowell
description:
Child reunited with family after he was detained by immigration agents in San Diego and transferred to Texas

An eight-year-old Haitian boy who was put into restraints and detained by immigration agents in San Diego on 4 November and transferred to a facility in Texas has been reunited with his family in California.

Representative Juan Vargas shared a photograph of the boy and his family in a social media post on Monda, writing: “11 days ago, an 8-year-old in San Diego was taken into federal custody during an immigration check-in. He was separated from his loved ones and held in a facility in Texas. Today, he’s finally home.”

Continue reading...
title: Eight-year-old Haitian boy returns home after release from ICE custody

author: Sam Levine
description:
Trump homeland security chief says ‘we still got to live our life’ amid outcry over journey to LSU on government plane

US homeland security secretary Markwayne Mullin has defended his decision to fly in a private government to a college football game on Saturday as Americans weathered widespread flight delays and cancellations, saying: “We still got to live our life.”

Mullin, a former US senator from Oklahoma, traveled on a government aircraft on Saturday to watch a football game between Louisiana State University and the University of Texas, the New York Post reported on Tuesday. The trip to Baton Rouge, Louisiana, came about a day after a four-hour ground stop that led to thousands of flights being
title: Markwayne Mullin defends private-jet trip to football game as millions hit by flight delays

author: George Chidi
description:
LaNeve, who served as Hegseth’s senior military commander, nominated to permanently replace Gen Randy George

Donald Trump has nominated Gen Chris LaNeve to be the US army’s top officer, making permanent his interim service after defense secretary Pete Hegseth unexpectedly fired his predecessor in April.

LaNeve had been serving as Hegseth’s senior military commander before his nomination for a fourth star and service as vice chief of staff of the army in February.

Continue reading...
title: Trump nominates Chris LaNeve as army chief after Hegseth fired predecessor

author: Guardian staff
description:
Foreign affairs minister Penny Wong says rapid expansion of settlements and settler violence are ‘extinguishing the possibility of a two-state solution’

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Australia has announced another tranche of sanctions on individuals and organisations involved in illegal settlement expansion and human rights abuses against Palestinians in the West Bank.

In a statement, the foreign affairs minister, Penny Wong, said it was the first time Australian sanctions had targeted a construction company involved in the building of settlements.

Continue reading...
title: Australia sanctions individuals and company involved in illegal West Bank settlements

author: Patrick Butler Social policy editor
description:
Milburn lays out sweeping aims and finer details for how to fix the Neets crisis – and is obsessive about welfare

  • Neet ideas: what’s in Milburn’s report?

It is not clear if too many people were expecting Everything Everywhere All at Once, but that is what Alan Milburn has delivered. From a Welfare State to a Working State is almost absurdly ambitious. The terms of reference said something about the drivers of youth labour markets. We got a blueprint for how to fix everything and everyone.

Wha
title: Milburn’s absurdly ambitious report offers blueprint for fixing everything and everyone

author: Tom Perkins
description:
Non-profit FracTracker Alliance alleges regulators have exempted compounds used in drilling despite 2022 law

The fossil-fuel industry is violating Colorado law by not disclosing which chemicals it uses in drilling, a new analysis by the FracTracker Alliance non-profit alleges, and state records show it has used illegal or dangerous compounds while fracking.

Drilling chemicals can include xylene, toluene, benzene, Pfas and other dangerous toxicants, industry records and literature from other regions show. A first-in-the-nation 2022 Colorado law requires fossil-fuel operators and their suppliers to make public all chemicals used in “downhole oil and gas production”. But regulators have exempted compounds used in drilling, claiming that dril
title: Fossil-fuel industry accused of violating Colorado law over not disclosing drilling chemicals

author: Maeve McClenaghan and Robyn Vinter
description:
Scale of cases in family court relating to Ahmadi Religion of Peace and Light ‘rarely seen before’, one lawyer said

Scores of children linked to a religious sect raided by police over allegations of serious sexual offences and modern slavery are now the subject of care proceedings, court documents have revealed.

Family courts were dealing with more than 40 cases in relation to “a very significant number of children” who were living at the compound run by the Ahmadi Religion of Peace and Light (AROPL) when it was raided by police in April.

Continue reading...
title: Children linked to religious sect raided by UK police now subject of care proceedings

author: Martin Pengelly
description:
Promise Me, America was published just before the former US president’s 84th birthday as he battles advanced cancer

In a new memoir, Joe Biden offers harsh criticism of Volodymyr Zelenskyy, who has led Ukraine through four-and-a-half years of war against Russia. According to Biden, the Ukrainian president was “difficult to work with”, “moody and stubborn in our private conversations”, and “not as grateful as I expected” for US diplomatic support and military aid.

Biden’s memoir, Promise Me, America, was published on Tuesday, shortly before his 84th birthday and as he battles advanced prostate cancer. Largely a trumpeting of achievements in office, with scant admission of failings ultimately crowned by his own party deeming him unfit fo
title: Joe Biden criticizes Zelenskyy as ‘moody’ and ‘not as grateful’ in new memoir

author: Cris Seda Chabrier
description:
High-stakes hearing comes in wake of resignation from Nvidia after alleged affair with suspected Chinese spy

Nvidia’s former CEO Jensen Huang will testify before several congressional committees on 1 December, setting the stage for a high-stakes hearing in the wake of his resignation following an affair with a suspected Chinese spy.

Tim Teter, Nvidia’s general counsel, has also agreed to appear for a closed-door transcribed interview the following day, 2 December.

Continue reading...
title: Jensen Huang to testify before Congress on ‘potential breach of national security’

author: Reuters
description:
Camilo Rodriguez’s death comes as the country grapples with a surge in drug violence

The Costa Rican journalist Camilo Rodriguez, who gained prominence for publishing allegations against ⁠suspected drug traffickers and politicians, was shot dead on Monday, authorities said.

The first known killing of a journalist ⁠in Costa Rica in ⁠25 years, ​Rodriguez’s death comes as the country grapples with a surge in drug violence driven by international trafficking groups, despite long ⁠being regarded as one of Central America’s most peaceful and stable democracies.

Continue reading...
title: Costa Rican journalist shot dead in first such killing in 25 years

author: Maya Yang
description:
Wreckage of Piper Comanche aircraft was found on Monday after going missing in park’s North Rim area

Three people were killed in a plane crash near the northern rim of Grand Canyon national park in Arizona, the federal park service said on Monday.

The Grand Canyon regional communications center received a report of a missing Piper Comanche aircraft at about 11.30pm on Sunday, a statement from officials said. The plane was last known to be in the Basin area of the park’s North Rim, a higher-elevation and less-visited section of the park.

Continue reading...
title: Three people killed in plane crash in Arizona’s Grand Canyon national park

author: Reuters
description:
The audits check whether financial statements ​are fairly presented and financial systems ‌and processes are sound

The Pentagon failed a financial audit for the ninth consecutive year, according to an inspector general ⁠report released on Monday – but an official said a majority of its units passed for the first time.

The US defense department chief financial officer, Jules Hurst, told ⁠Reuters an independent auditor ⁠found that ​financial statements for 14 of the Pentagon’s 25 standalone reporting entities passed in the 2026 fiscal year, which ended in September, up from ⁠11 the prior year. Those entities account for 56% of the department’s assets – and 86% of its liabilities.

Continue reading...
title: US Pentagon fails ninth straight audit despite progress in organizing finances

author: Lex McMenamin
description:
New Jersey university’s Republicans club invited Bovino, who oversaw Trump’s ICE surges, to speak on campus

Hundreds protested outside a Rutgers University campus building on Monday night, jeering former border patrol commander Greg Bovino, who was inside addressing a crowd of about 25 people.

The university’s Republicans club had invited Bovino to speak, calling him the “Great Commander” and the “GOAT” in social posts promoting the event at the New Brunswick, New Jersey, campus. During the two-hour talk, the room never quite filled up, occupied mostly by journalists, club members and other students criticizing the former border patrol chief.

Continue reading...
title: Hundreds protest against ex-border patrol chief Greg Bovino at Rutgers University talk

author: Josh Butler
description:
Music legend is joined by Jimmy Barnes and Peter Garrett in backing Not AI’s To Take campaign ahead of Aria awards

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Australia’s creative community has launched a major campaign pleading with the Albanese government not to water down copyright law amid furious lobbying from AI companies, ahead of Wednesday night’s Aria awards.

Music legends Jimmy Barnes, Paul Kelly and Peter Garrett are among those backing the Not AI’s To Take campaign, supported by dozens of creative groups representing the recording, writing, publishing, film, television and media industries.
title: Paul Kelly pleads for Albanese to ‘show some backbone’ over AI as creatives campaign for copyright protections

author: Penry Buckley
description:
From train timetables to coffee cups and property underquoting, the NSW premier is making policy reversals well ahead of the March election

  • Get our daily political email, free app or daily news podcast

If recent coverage is to be believed, the New South Wales premier, Chris Minns, is a talented gymnast. A last-minute intervention by the premier on Monday afternoon, the day before a suite of reforms on underquoting were due to take effect, marks a quadruple or quintuple policy “backflip” by Minns in recent weeks, depending on who you ask.

The laws banning real estate agents from lowering the adve
title: Chris Minns’ backflips are adding up. Is he ‘clearing the runway’ or panicking?

author: Luca Ittimani
description:
Men still dominate top-paid positions but businesses’ ‘deliberate’ decisions have narrowed gap, workplace gender equality agency report finds

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Australian women earn 80c for every $1 men earn, on average, after Australia’s gender pay gap fell below 20% for the first time in 2025-26.

The workplace gender equality agency’s (WGEA) report on Wednesday showed men still dominated top-paid positions but businesses’ decisions have narrowed the gap.

Continue reading...
title: Australia’s gender pay gap falls below 20% for first time

author: Associated Press
description:
More than 40 US states have passed laws restricting phones at schools with goal of boosting students’ focus and learning

A large-scale study published Tuesday found strict cellphone restrictions in US schools – ones that require students to put phones in locked pouches for the entire academic day – result in small academic gains.

And there could be further gains if schools continue banning phones, the researchers said.

Continue reading...
title: School phone bans result in ‘modest’ academic gains for students, study shows

author: Joanna Partridge
description:
News of Spanish-owned lender’s policy emerges as other banks are toughening their stance on working from home

  • Business live – latest updates

Staff at the high street bank Santander have been permitted to log holiday and sick leave as days worked in the office, helping them to meet workplace attendance requirements.

Back-office staff at the Spanish-owned lender have been expected to spend at least 12 working days each month in what the company calls a “head office location”, although this does not apply to staff working in bank branches.

Continue
title: Santander allows staff to count holidays and sick leave as days worked in office

author: Benita Kolovos
description:
Ben Carroll, Jess Wilson, Ellen Sandell and Warren Pickering grilled by undecided voters – and each other – as state prepares to head to the polls

For a brief moment on Tuesday night, the Victorian election looked like it might actually get interesting.

Two weeks into the offical campaign, with early voting opening on Wednesday, the contest has been pretty short on excitement. The Labor government has continued to slide in the polls, while the Coalition opposition has largely been focused on not getting in its own way for long enough to cruise to victory.
title: Voldemort, Gotham City and the Greens: Victorian election gets a jolt of life as leaders face off in sole debate

author: Martin Belam
description:
Blow to Kremlin as prestigious bridge linking occupied Ukrainian peninsula struck by missile. Plus, what is in store for Robert Pattinson, the new 007?

Good morning. Ukraine has critically damaged the Kerch bridge linking occupied Crimea with Russia in an overnight missile attack, in what Ukrainian officials say is a symbolic blow to the Kremlin. The strike follows an earlier attack on Monday that targeted an arch across its central section.

Ukraine has declared that the Kerch bridge, built eight years ago after Vladimir Putin’s 2014 annexation of Crimea, is illegal. It has repeatedly attempted to destroy it. The Kremlin-appointed governor of Crimea, Sergey Aksyonov, confirmed that the bridge, which was temporarily closed on Monday, was no longer usable. Photos suggest that a 227-metre road arch span has fallen into the Kerch strait.

You c
title: Bridge between Russia and occupied Crimea ‘no longer usable’ after Kyiv strike | First Thing

author: Ramon Antonio Vargas in New Orleans
description:
Police say David Hyde, 68, left with shoe prints in face from kicks to head and prescription medication stolen in attack

A man who was unhoused and “unable to defend himself due to health issues” was recently beaten to death and had his prescription medication taken outside a pharmacy in New Orleans, according to authorities.

The killing of 68-year-old David Hyde led police to arrest Antonio Myles, 19, on a count of second-degree murder, with investigators alleging that they came to suspect the much younger man after he had bragged to others about fatally beating an unhoused person.

Continue reading...
title: New Orleans police arrest teen over beating death of homeless man ‘unable to defend himself’

author: Mark Sweney
description:
Modella Capital plans auction of high street retailer, which employs about 3,500 people, next year

  • Business live – latest updates

The owner of TG Jones is exploring a potential sale less than 18 months after completing a deal to buy the high street chain formerly known as WH Smith.

Modella Capital, which also owns businesses including Hobbycraft, completed a deal to buy the 233-year-old business for £76m in June last year.

Continue reading..
title: Former WH Smith chain TG Jones put up for sale after closing 130 stores

author: Jakub Krupa
description:
Kyiv and Moscow dispute scale of damage which means travel out of the peninsula is now only via a land corridor vulnerable to Ukrainian drone attack

Ukraine critically damages Kerch bridge

I am also keeping an eye on an incident in the Czech capital of Prague where two commuter trains collided near the main train station, leaving 46 injured, including four seriously.

The two passenger trains collided on an overpass while travelling at a low speed around 7am this morning, according to the Czech media.

Continue reading...
title: Ukraine hails attack on vital Kerch bridge linking Russia and Crimea – Europe live

author: Sarah Basford Canales
description:
Crossbenchers say the proposals could allow an ‘uncapped amount of money’ to flow to major parties through investment funds

  • Get our daily political email, free app or daily news podcast

Independent MPs say the government’s last-minute changes to controversial election funding laws would allow “an uncapped amount of money” to flow to the major parties through investment funds.

The amendments to the incoming federal electoral laws, which the government describes as “technical”, were introduced on Tuesday afternoon and come weeks before they are set to begin operating.
title: ‘Line their own coffers’: independent MPs lambast Labor’s last-minute changes to election funding laws

author: Amanda Meade Media correspondent
description:
Documents show draft Acma reports backed reporting of Gold Walkley award-winning journalist Mark Willacy about Australian War Memorial

  • Sign up for Guardian Australia’s free weekly media newsletter here

An investigation by staff of the Australian Media and Communications Authority (Acma) cleared an ABC Four Corners program over its War Memorial reporting – only for the draft report findings to be reversed by the regulator’s leadership, documents released under freedom of information reveal.

Internal correspondence shows the 11th hour backflip forced a “retrofit” of the report which initially said: “Staff are of the preliminary view that the program did not breach the impartiality provision of the [ABC] code [of conduct] with respect to this allegation.”
title: Communications watchdog leadership reversed findings of draft report into ABC Four Corners program, FoI documents reveal

author: Phillip Inman
description:
Wage growth falls to 3.5% in September, as ministers examine how best to get young people into work

  • Milburn urges Burnham to spend billions on young people

  • Who are the Neets? UK youth job crisis in five charts

  • Business live – latest updates

The UK unemployment rate has unexpectedly fallen as the government prepares to release a major report on the youth jobs crisis.

The unemployment rate was 4.6% in September, dipping from 4.7% in
title: UK unemployment unexpectedly eases to 4.6%, as government prepares to release Milburn report

author: Douglas Smith Indigenous affairs reporter
description:
The NSW transport department says passenger safety is its ‘highest priority’ and the driver is no longer employed by the operator

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Transport for NSW is investigating allegations that a young Aboriginal mother and her family were told to leave a bus and left by the side of a regional highway because her 22-month-old child was crying.

Wiradjuri woman Kaneesha Lee Williams was travelling home from Sydney to the Riverina town of Darlington Point, 155km west of Wagga Wagga, with her young daughter, Audria, and her mother, Tamara, on Sunday.

Continue reading...
title: Aboriginal mother allegedly kicked off a bus in regional NSW because her baby was crying

author: Australian Associated Press
description:
Bikie Joel Leavitt, who has a criminal history including riot, affray and assaulting police, tells inquiry he can’t recall why union was pushing for him

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

A bikie and former CFMEU member says he can’t recall why union representatives were pushing hard to have him hired on a construction project.

Bandidos member Joel Leavitt gave evidence to the royal commission into alleged corruption across Victoria’s construction sector on Tuesday.

Continue reading...
title: CFMEU pushed to get notorious Bandidos member hired on construction project, Big Build royal commission hears

author: Ben Smee Queensland state correspondent
description:
Fitness influencer’s lawyer calls comment during taped conversation between client and his father ‘ill-judged’ but denies it amounts to a suggestion of interfering with a witness

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

A Queensland court has been played a prison recording of the former Bachelor star Sam Wood sobbing as he tells his father that he needs to talk to his wife, Snezana, and that his domestic violence charges would be dropped if she recanted her statements to police.

The court of appeal is hearing a third application by Wood, 46, for bail over allegations he strangled and assaulted his wife while the fa
title: ‘Let me talk to Snez’: court hears recording of Sam Wood saying wife Snezana could recant domestic violence allegations

author: Associated Press
description:
Labor leader was remembered for her advocacy and co-founding union that would become United Farm Workers

California officials paid tribute to Dolores Huerta, one of the nation’s most influential labor leaders, civil rights icons and feminist activists, at a memorial ceremony Monday at the state capitol.

They remembered her as a relentless advocate for a more just and fair world. Huerta co-founded a union that became the United Farm Workers with César Chávez and made famous her rallying cry, “Sí, se puede!” – which translates to “Yes, it can be done!”

Continue reading...
title: Dolores Huerta honored in ceremony at California state capitol

author: Jonathan Barrett Business editor
description:
Creditors meeting hears upmarket retailer owes $11m to employees and recorded a net loss of $228m last financial year

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Upmarket retailer David Jones collapsed into administration earlier this month owing well over $400m, after accelerating financial losses and reputational damage threatened its ability to stock shelves for Christmas.

About 500 creditors attended its first meeting on Tuesday, where administrators McGrathNicol broke down the 188-year-old chain’s massive debt pile, including an estimated $180m owed to suppliers and $11m to employees.

Continue reading...
title: David Jones’ total debt is over $400m including millions owed to staff, administrators confirm

author: Josh Taylor Technology reporter
description:
Toll employee Ricardo Martins Silva used smartglasses to take photos at an LPG terminal despite the risk of an explosion caused by an electrical spark, a court heard

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

A Toll truck driver was fired from work in Victoria after using smartglasses to snap photos at an LPG terminal, in what was described as an “intrinsically unsafe” incident.

It is the first reported case in Australia of a worker dismissed for using smartglasses in a workplace.

Continue reading...
title: Truck driver fired for ‘unsafe’ use of smartglasses in first reported sacking over device in Australia
